entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The state has filed this appeal challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Reference Court under Section 28A (3) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

The reference is answered in favour of the claimants redetermining the land value at the rate of Rs. 5,500/- per Are relying on Ext. A1 judgment dated 07.04.2000 in L.A.R No.170/1994 of the Sub Court, Kollam, finding that the subject land and Ext.A1 land were acquired as per the same Section 4(1) Notification dated 29.11.1981.
2.
The Land Acquisition Officer passed an award fixing the land value at Rs. 1,472 per Are.

In L.A.R.
No. 170/1994, the Reference Court passed an award dated 07.04.2000 fixing the land value at the rate of Rs. 5,500/- per Are.

Thereupon, the claimant filed an Application under Section 2025:KER:39411 LA.APP. NO. 191 OF 2019 28A of the Land Acquisition Act to the District Collector claiming the same rate of land value which is fixed in L.A.R. No. 170/1994.
The said Application was rejected by the collector as per order dated 15.07.2013, on the ground that the landowner had accepted the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.
The claimant sought reference to the Reference Court, and accordingly, the present reference was made and the same was answered by the Reference Court.
3. I heard the learned Senior Government Pleader for the appellant, Smt. Rekha C. Nair and also the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants, Sri. Siju Kamalasanan.

4. The learned Senior Government Pleader cited the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Union of India v. Raghubir Singh (Dead) by LRs. [(1989) 2 SCC 754] in 2025:KER:39411 LA.APP.
NO. 191 OF 2019 which it is held that the Amendment Act of the year 1984 is applicable only in the case of awards passed after the cut- off date of 30.04.1982 on the ground that the Bill was presented on 30.04.1982.

entities.text: Union of India v. Raghubir Singh (Dead) by LRs. [(1989) 2 SCC 754]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand, the award was passed on 28.04.1982 and hence the claimant is not entitled to submit an Application under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act.

The learned Senior Government Pleader pointed out that in the said decision, even though the question of entitlement of higher solatium alone was considered, it is specifically held that the benefit of the amended provision will be available only with effect from 30.04.1982.
Hence, the benefit under Section 28A could be made available only with respect to awards passed from 30.04.1982.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants cited the decision of this Court in 2025:KER:39411 LA.APP. NO. 191 OF 2019 Louis Joyi v. State of Kerala [1997 (1) KLT 762]
and the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Babua Ram v. State of Uttar Pradesh [(1995) 2 SCC 689] and contended that even if awards are passed before the cut- off date, the relevant is the date of the award of the Reference Court on which the claimant relies for filing application under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act.

entities.text: Louis Joyi v. State of Kerala [1997 (1) KLT 762]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Babua Ram v. State of Uttar Pradesh [(1995) 2 SCC 689]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the date of award of the judgment relied on in the Application under Section 28A is after the cut-off date, the claimants are entitled to maintain the Application.
In the case on hand the relied judgment is after the cut-off date.
6. I have considered the rival contentions.
7. On going through the decision in Raghubir Singh (supra), it is seen that the issue involved in the said case is with regard to the entitlement of the higher solatium as per the Amendment Act.

In the said decision, the Hon'ble 2025:KER:39411 LA.APP. NO. 191 OF 2019 Supreme Court held that even though the Act was implemented on 24.09.1984, the land owners will be entitled to claim with respect to the awards with effect from 30.04.1982 as the Bill was presented on that day.
It is specifically held that with respect to awards passed before 30.04.1982, the claimants are not entitled to get compensation.
In the judgment of this Court in Louis Joyi (Supra), this Court has considered a case in which an award was passed before 30.04.1982 and hence Section 28A Application was rejected on that ground.
This Court specifically held that the relevant date is the date of the award relied on for the entitlement of the claimant to make a claim under Section 28A.
If the relied-on award is after the coming into force of Section 28A, the land owner is entitled to claim benefits under Section 28A.

In the said decision, it is not specifically considered as to whether the 2025:KER:39411 LA.APP. NO. 191 OF 2019 benefits under Section 28A would be available with respect to awards passed before 30.04.1982.
But the fact is that in the said case also the award was passed before 30.04.1982.

But in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Babu Ram (supra) it is held that an award under Section 11 made prior to 24.09.1984 and a reference under Section 18 sought and secured was pending in the civil court on 24.09.1984 and civil court determines higher compensation on or after 24.09.1984, persons interested in other land covered by the same Notification under Section 4(1), would be entitled to make an application/applications in writing to the Collector to redetermine the compensation and to make an award under Section 28A(2) on the basis of the award and decree under Section 26.

In view of the said proposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case 2025:KER:39411 LA.APP. NO. 191 OF 2019 arising from Section 28A Application, I am of the view that the claimants in this case are also entitled to maintain their Section 28A Application.
Accordingly, I do not find any ground or reason to interfere with the finding of the Reference Court that the claimant is entitled to the benefits under Section 28A.
The Land Acquisition Appeal is dismissed.

Sd/-
